He played nine seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) between 2005 and 2014 before playing overseas. He played [[high school basketball]] at [[Henninger High School]] and [[South Kent School]] before he was drafted in the second round of the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]]. Born in New York and an American by birth, Blatche became a naturalized citizen of the Philippines in June 2014, enabling him to join the country's [[Philippines men's national basketball team|national basketball team]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.spin.ph/sports/pba/news/andray-blatche-now-eligible-to-play-for-gilas-as-president-aquino-signs-naturalization-papers-v02 |title=Andray Blatche now eligible to play for Gilas as President Aquino signs naturalization papers |access-date=June 11, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031135108/http://www.spin.ph/sports/pba/news/andray-blatche-now-eligible-to-play-for-gilas-as-president-aquino-signs-naturalization-papers-v02 |archive-date=October 31, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}{{Cite web|title=Andray Blatche {{!}} Brooklyn {{!}} National Basketball Association {{!}} Yahoo! Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/players/3975/|access-date=2020-12-18|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en-US}} ==High school career== Blatche spent four years at [[Henninger High School]] in [[Syracuse, New York]] and then an [[Super senior|extra year]] at the [[South Kent School]] in [[South Kent, Connecticut]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2172615 Blatche in good condition after being shot in carjacking] He averaged 27.5 points, 16.0 rebounds and 6.0 blocks per game during his fifth-year campaign in 2004–05 as he guided South Kent to a 32–9 record.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andray_blatche/bio/ |title=Andray Blatche Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=August 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140816005916/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andray_blatche/bio/ |archive-date=August 16, 2014 |url-status=dead }} Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Blatche was listed as the No. 2 power forward and the No. 4 player in the nation in 2005.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Andray-Blatche-19485;_ylt=Ah3RbrcNXt6RWmMzVk14JBRGPZB4 Andray Blatche Recruiting Profile] He declared for the [[2005 NBA draft]] out of [[prep-to-pro|high school]], and while originally thought of as a first-round prospect, he slipped to the second round and was taken by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 49th overall pick.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2979614 Wizards re-sign forward Blatche to multiyear deal] ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2005–2012)=== Blatche was shot in a [[carjacking]] on September 25, 2005, and as a result missed training camp. He recovered successfully and played his first game with Washington versus [[Seattle SuperSonics|Seattle]] on November 11, 2005, scoring five points in a 137–96 Wizards victory.[https://web.archive.org/web/20121025115759/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=251111027 Arenas scores 32 as Wizards look Super against Sonics] On December 14, 2005, he was assigned to the [[Roanoke Dazzle]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. On January 2, 2006, he was recalled by the Wizards. He finished the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]] only playing in 29 games for the Wizards, averaging 2.3 points and 1.3 rebounds. With the injuries to Wizards' [[Center (basketball)|centers]] [[Etan Thomas]] and [[Michael Ruffin]], Blatche was occasionally pressed into service as a backup center in the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]]. On August 17, 2007, Blatche re-signed with the Wizards to a multi-year deal.[http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/blatche_070817.html Wizards Re-Sign Forward Andray Blatche] During the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], Blatche continued showing improvement, and with center [[Etan Thomas]] out with a season-ending heart condition, his minutes increased. At the end of the season, Blatche played in every game for the Wizards, starting 15, averaging 8.2 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.4 blocks.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/blatcan01/gamelog/2008/ Andray Blatche 2007-08 Game Log] [[File:Andray Blatche.jpg|thumbnail|left|Blatche with the [[Washington Wizards|Wizards]]]] On January 9, 2010, Blatche was fined $10,000 by the Wizards for participating in [[Gilbert Arenas]]' mimicking gunplay before a game on January 5, 2010, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Arenas was being investigated for a prior incident involving guns in the Wizards' locker room, but made light of the accusations by pointing his finger at his teammates, as if he were shooting them. His teammates were photographed smiling and laughing with him.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4810297 Wiz fine Blatche, McGee, Foye, Young] [[File:Andray Blatche and Chris Bosh.jpg|thumbnail|left|Blatche shooting over [[Chris Bosh]]]] On February 28, 2010, he scored a career high 36 points on 17–31 shooting during the Wizards' 89–85 victory against the [[New Jersey Nets]]. Blatche continued to be the starter on the team, and his stats significantly improved. Blatche just missed a triple-double as he had 20 points, a career-high 13 assists, nine rebounds and two steals in the Wizards' 109–99 victory over the [[New Jersey Nets]] on April 4.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/blatcan01/gamelog/2010/ Andray Blatche 2009-10 Game Log] In September 2010, he signed a veteran extension with the Wizards. The [[2010–11 NBA season]] was a career year for Blatche, with 63 starts in 64 games played, and career highs in points (16.8), rebounds (8.2), assists (2.3) and steals (1.5). On March 20, 2012, the Wizards announced that they were benching Blatche indefinitely due to lack of conditioning,{{cite news |title=Wizards plan to sit Andray Blatche until he gets in better shape |date=2012-03-20 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727055231/https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-plan-to-sit-andray-blatche-until-he-gets-in-better-shape/2012/03/20/gIQAi9rxPS_blog.html |archive-date=2021-07-27 |url-status=live |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-plan-to-sit-andray-blatche-until-he-gets-in-better-shape/2012/03/20/gIQAi9rxPS_blog.html}} and on July 16, he was waived via the amnesty clause.[http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-waive-blatche WIZARDS WAIVE BLATCHE] Blatche would later be vocal about his treatment by the Wizards organization, stating, "When things weren't starting well, they used me as an excuse." He also claimed that the management deliberately tried to ruin his career: "For them to say, ‘Oh, he's a bad teammate. He's a cancer in the locker room.’ He's this and that. All that was a bunch of lies! A bunch of lies. That's what really made me mad. That showed me, they tried to end me."[http://www.bulletsforever.com/2012/11/27/3697088/andray-blatche-radio-interview-washington-wizards Highlights from Andray Blatche's crazy radio interview] Coach [[Randy Wittman]] responded to the allegations by saying, "I’m not going to get into that. We did everything we could to help him, as we will with every player that ever comes here."{{cite news| last=Lee | first=Michael | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/wp/2012/11/27/andray-blatche-on-wizards-they-tried-to-end-me/ | title=Andray Blatche on Wizards: "They tried to end me" | work=WashingtonPost.com | date=November 27, 2012 |access-date=November 27, 2012}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2012–2014)=== [[File:Blatche live.jpg|thumbnail|right|Blatche taking a jump shot over [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]].]] On September 12, 2012, Blatche signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10917 |title=Brooklyn Nets sign Andray Blatche |access-date=September 13, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140321042511/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10917 |archive-date=March 21, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} After Blatche signed with the Nets, he decided to wear number 0. "Zero reminds of me how everybody gave up on me", he said.{{cite news| last=Lee | first=Michael | title=Andray Blatche: 'I'm blessed to be here with a second chance'|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/wp/2012/10/15/andray-blatche-im-blessed-to-be-here-with-a-second-chance/|work=WashingtonPost.com|date=October 15, 2012|access-date=June 17, 2013}} When [[Brook Lopez]] injured his foot, Blatche was given the chance to start in his absence. Without Lopez, the Nets struggled with a 2–5 record.{{cite web|last=Kline|first=Brandon|title=Brook Lopez injury update: Nets' center could return tonight vs. Pistons|url=http://newyork.sbnation.com/2012/12/14/3767190/brook-lopez-injury-update-brooklyn-nets-detroit-pistons-game-time-tv|work=SBNation.com|date=December 14, 2012|access-date=December 14, 2012}} Despite the Nets' struggles without Lopez, Blatche played well, averaging 18.1 points and 8.8 rebounds.{{cite news|last=Cacciola|first=Scott|title=Don't Blame Blatche For the Nets' Descent|url=https://www.wsj.com/news/articles/SB10001424127887324481204578175592174082384|work=WSJ.com|date=December 12, 2012|access-date=December 12, 2012}} On January 4, 2013, Blatche made his return to the [[Capital One Arena|Verizon Center]] and was playing the [[Washington Wizards]]. When Blatche entered that game in the first quarter, he was booed heartily by the fans in attendance. In 19 minutes of game action, Blatche had 13 points and 12 rebounds.{{cite web|title=Andray Blatche returns to Washington, receives boos as expected (VIDEO)|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/01/04/andray-blatche-returns-to-washington-receives-boos-as-expected-video/|work=NBCSports.com|date=January 4, 2013|access-date=January 4, 2013}} Blatche played in all 82 regular season games in 2012–13, averaging 10.3 points and 5.1 rebounds and set a career high in field goal percentage (51.2%). Blatche also played in seven playoff games for the Nets and averaged 10.3 points and 4.9 rebounds. On July 11, 2013, Blatche re-signed with the Nets.[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-re-sign-andray-blatche Nets Re-Sign Andray Blatche] In December 2013, starting center [[Brook Lopez]] went down with a season-ending foot injury, increasing Blatche's minutes. In the first game without Lopez, Blatche had 11 points and seven rebounds in 25 minutes of action in a loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite news|title=Brook Lopez injury could be fatal blow to Brooklyn Nets season|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/lawrence-lopez-nets-hope-article-1.1557060|work=New York Daily News|date=December 23, 2013|access-date=December 23, 2013}} On June 20, 2014, Blatche opted out of his contract with the Nets, thus becoming an unrestricted free agent.[https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/brooklyn-nets/post/_/id/19405/agent-blatche-opts-out-is-a-free-agent Agent: Blatche opts out, is a free agent] ===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2014–2018)=== On September 20, 2014, Blatche signed a one-year, $2.5 million contract with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/135258/andray-blatche-officially-signs-with-xinjiang-flying-tigers.html Andray Blatche officially signs with Xinjiang Flying Tigers] Following the conclusion of the [[2014–15 CBA season|2014–15 CBA regular season]], Blatche terminated his contract with Xinjiang on February 1, 2015.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/150756/the-complete-list-of-players-available-from-china.html The complete list of players available from China] In 38 games, he averaged 31.1 points, 14.6 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.8 steals per game.{{cite news|last1=Henson|first1=Joaquin|title=Andray back to NBA?|url=http://www.philstar.com/sports/2015/02/08/1421437/andray-back-nba|access-date=February 9, 2015|work=PhilStar.com|date=February 8, 2015}} In March 2015, Blatche re-signed with Xinjiang on a three-year, $7.5 million contract.{{cite news|last=Feldman|first=Dan|title=Report: Andray Blatche signs three-year deal in China|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/03/23/report-andray-blatche-signs-three-year-deal-in-china/|access-date=March 24, 2015|work=NBCSports.com|date=March 23, 2015}}{{cite news|title=Gilas star Andray Blatche's new contract in China reportedly worth $7.5M|url=http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/gilas-star-andray-blatches-new-contract-in-china-reportedly-worth-7-5m|access-date=March 24, 2015|work=InterAksyon.com|date=March 24, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326231402/http://www.interaksyon.com/interaktv/gilas-star-andray-blatches-new-contract-in-china-reportedly-worth-7-5m|archive-date=March 26, 2015}} In November 2016, Blatche sustained an injury and was subsequently replaced on the roster temporarily by [[Ben Bentil]].[http://www.celticslife.com/2016/11/former-celtic-draftee-ben-bentil-signs.html Former Celtic draftee Ben Bentil signs with Chinese team Xinjiang] He returned to action in late December and went on to lead Xinjiang to the CBA Finals, where they swept the series against the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] 4–0 to claim the championship. On January 4, 2018, it was announced that [[Augusto Lima]] was taking Blatche's spot on the roster. Blatche was criticized for his poor performance and negative attitude during the early stages of the 2017–18 season. He averaged 12.8 points and 6.4 rebounds in the five games he played, and had a negative impact on the team's defensive efforts.{{cite web|url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-01/04/c_136871220.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104063414/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-01/04/c_136871220.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 4, 2018|title=CBA side Xinjiang to replace Blatche with Brazilian center Augusto Lima|work=xinhuanet.com|date=January 4, 2018|access-date=January 4, 2018}} He returned to the team in March 2018 for their playoff series against Guangdong. ===Tianjin Gold Lions (2018–2019)=== In December 2018, Blatche signed with the [[Tianjin Gold Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite news|title=Andray Blatche signs at Gold Lions|url=https://basketball.asia-basket.com/China/news/558994/Andray-Blatche-signs-at-Gold-Lions|date=December 19, 2018|work=asia-basket.com|access-date=December 28, 2018}}{{cite news|title=官宣！布莱切加盟天津男篮 顶替阿尔德里奇|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/basketball/cba/2018-12-27/doc-ihqhqcis0899223.shtml|language=zh|date=December 27, 2018|work=sina.com.cn|access-date=December 28, 2018}} In 19 games, he averaged 20.7 points, 11.0 rebounds, 4.1 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.8 blocks per game. ===Later years (2020–2025)=== Blatche played in the 2020 Dubai Basketball International Championship with non-league Philippine-based team [[Mighty Sports]]. He helped Mighty clinch the title in the club tournament held in the United Arab Emirates.{{cite news |last1=Lozada |first1=Bong |title=Former Gilas center Andray Blatche tweets desire to play in PBA |url=https://sports.inquirer.net/445739/former-gilas-center-andray-blatche-tweets-desire-to-play-in-pba |access-date=19 January 2024 |work=Philippine Daily Inquirer |date=27 December 2021 |language=en}} In 2021, he expressed interest to join the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). Despite having Filipino citizenship by this time, naturalized players like himself are still considered as imports. Imports are also subject to height cap restriction. Blatche joined [[Strong Group Athletics (basketball)|Strong Group Athletics]] (SGA), another non-league Philippine-based side, for the [[Dubai]] International Basketball Championship in 2024. By this time Blatche has given up on his prospect of playing in the PBA.{{cite news |last1=Ramos |first1=Gerry |title=Andray Blatche says he has given up hope of playing in PBA |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/blatche-says-he-has-given-up-hope-to-play-in-pba-a793-20240112 |access-date=19 January 2024 |work=Sports Interactive Network Philippines |date=13 January 2024 |language=en}} He rejoined SGA for the 2025 edition of the tournament.{{cite news |last1=Terrado |first1=Reuben |title=Andray Blatche to retire after one last tour with SGA in Dubai |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/andray-blatche-to-retire-after-one-last-tour-with-sga-in-dubai-a795-20250111 |access-date=12 January 2025 |work=Sports Interactive Network Philippines |date=11 January 2025 |language=en}} Blatche has announced his retirement in February 2025.{{Cite web |last=Suing |first=Ivan |date=2025-02-25 |title=Blatche calls it a pro career |.546 |.378 |.743 |10.91 |4.3 |2.4 |1.1 |25.6 |- |} ==National team career== [[File:Andray Blatche World Cup 2014 (2).jpg|250px|thumb|Blatche with the [[Philippines men's national basketball team|Philippine national team]] at the 2014 FIBA World Cup.]] In January 2014, Blatche was asked by the [[Philippines men's national basketball team|Gilas Pilipinas]] to take part as a naturalized player for the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in Spain and the [[2014 Asian Games]] in [[Incheon]], [[South Korea]]. On May 26, 2014, a bill granting Blatche's Filipino citizenship was approved by the [[Senate of the Philippines|Philippine Senate]].[http://www.philstar.com/sports/2014/05/26/1327522/senate-grants-filipino-citizenship-nba-center-andray-blatche Senate grants Filipino citizenship to NBA center Andray Blatche] On June 11, 2014, Blatche officially became a Filipino citizen upon the signing of Republic Act 10636 by Philippine President [[Benigno Aquino III]]. In August 2014, Blatche was named in the 2014 Philippine FIBA Basketball World Cup and Asian Games squad.[http://www.arabnews.com/news/sports/615636 Lee, Dillinger, Blatche named to Gilas Asian Games team][http://www.sportando.com/en/national-teams/national-teams/133046/blatche-says-philippines-will-continue-to-impress-in-fiba-world-cup.html Blatche says Philippines will continue to impress in FIBA World Cup] He was later disqualified to play in the [[Basketball at the 2014 Asian Games|2014 Asian Games]] due to eligibility issues cited by the [[Olympic Council of Asia]] (OCA), as he lacked the required three-year residency in the Philippines.[https://www.rappler.com/sports/gilas-pilipinas/64953-why-andray-blatche-might-not-play-asian-games/ Why Andray Blatche might not play in the 2014 Asian Games][http://sports.inquirer.net/163726/its-final-blatche-out-of-asian-games It’s final: Blatche out of Asian Games]{{Cite web |url=http://basketballbuddha.com/andray-blatche-officially-disqualified-from-asian-games/ |title=Andray Blatche officially disqualified from Asian Games |access-date=October 31, 2014 |archive-date=September 15, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140915060253/http://basketballbuddha.com/andray-blatche-officially-disqualified-from-asian-games/ |url-status=dead }} In five games at the World Cup, he averaged 21.2 points, 13.8 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game.[https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Andray-Blatche 2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup – Andray Blatche] With an 18-point, 14-rebound performance, Blatche helped the Philippines to their first World Cup win in 40 years, defeating Senegal 81–79 in overtime.[http://www.nba.com/2014/news/09/04/philippines-makes-progress-world-cup.ap/index.html Philippines gets 1st World Cup win in 40 years] In 2015, Blatche played for the Philippines at the [[2015 FIBA Asia Championship]] under new head coach [[Tab Baldwin]]. In nine games, he averaged 17.8 points, 9.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170327104700/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/115697/sid/8072/tid/346/_/2015_FIBA_Asia_Championship/index.html 2015 FIBA Asia Championship – Andray Blatche] The following year, the team competed in the [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Manila|FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament]], where in two games, he scored a total of 51 points.[https://www.fiba.basketball/oqt/philippines/2016/player/Andray-Blatche 2016 FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Andray Blatche] Blatche was expected to suit up for the [[2017 FIBA Asia Cup]] but pulled out due to security concerns over the militant situation in the host country [[Lebanon]].{{cite web|last1=Catacutan|first1=Dodo|title=Andray Blatche unlikely to join Gilas in Fiba Asia Cup |url=https://www.rappler.com/sports/gilas-pilipinas/248514-philippine-team-sbp-moving-on-from-blatche/ |work=Rappler |date=4 January 2020}} ==Personal life== On the Sunday morning of September 25, 2005, three months after the Wizards selected him with the 49th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft|NBA draft]], Blatche was shot in an attempted [[carjacking]] that took place near his home in [[Alexandria, Virginia]]. Police said Blatche was ordered out of the car by men who emerged from a van and was shot before he could fully exit. Blatche's mother, Angela Oliver, said he was shot once in the chest, but that the bullet did not hit any vital organs. He was released from hospital two days later.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2174281 Blatche out of hospital after attempted carjacking] As a result of his injuries, he missed the Wizards' training camp,[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2175169 Blatche to miss training camp after being shot] although he could walk on his own three days after the shooting and one day after being released from the hospital. On August 2, 2007, Blatche was charged with sexual [[solicitation]] in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. after allegedly soliciting sex from an [[undercover]] police officer. The solicitation charge was dropped after Blatche followed court orders and attended a day-long seminar for men who solicit prostitutes.[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/08/31/AR2007083101038.html Blatche To Attend 'John School'] Blatche was arrested on June 4, 2008, in [[Virginia]] on charges of [[reckless driving]] and driving on a suspended license for the third time. Blatche was going 86 mph in a 70 mph zone in a [[Mercedes-Benz|Mercedes]] on [[Interstate 85]]. He was released on [[Bail bond|bond]].[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/06/04/AR2008060404281.html Wizards' Blatche Arrested] In June 2011, Blatche established the ''Andray Blatche Foundation'' and went on a charity mission to [[Jamaica]] where he donated sneakers, basketballs and gave a $50,000 check to Jamaican schools.{{cite news |title=Andray Blatche to go on charity mission to Jamaica |date=2011-06-29 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802170312/https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/andray-blatche-to-go-on-charity-mission-to-jamaica/2011/06/29/AGbZT3qH_blog.html |archive-date=2017-08-02 |url-status=live |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/andray-blatche-to-go-on-charity-mission-to-jamaica/2011/06/29/AGbZT3qH_blog.html}} ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons category|Andray Blatche}} {{basketballstats|nba=101154|bbr=b/blatcan01}} *{{Official website|http://www.andrayblatche007.com}} *[https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Andray-Blatche FIBA player profile] {{Navboxes|list= {{Jordan Brand Classic All-American Boys Game MVP}} {{2005 NBA draft}} {{China Kashgar 2016 FIBA Asia Champions Cup Winners}} }} {{navboxes |title=Philippines squad | titlestyle = background:#0038A8;
